note: Expectations validate the general rule set. A failure is a prompt to fix the rules or add a reviewed override, never to special-case the traversal.

cases.name: nightshade - spec golden case, both hierarchies unioned
cases.reject_note: black and white pepper are Piper nigrum (Piperaceae), not nightshades. The spec listed them in error; they are negatives, not misses.

cases.name: walnut - novel case, tree nut, not tuned against
peanut - novel case, legume, not tuned against
shellfish - novel case, animal branch, not tuned against
INVARIANT corn does not reach wheat
cases.reject_note: shared Poaceae ancestor, and the much nearer shared parents starch-producing plant / oil-producing plant / sugar-producing plant

cases.name: INVARIANT wheat does not reach corn
REGRESSION soy does not reach lobster via part_of
cases.reject_note: part_of was drafted as `forward`, which walked soybean plant -> soybean oil (flavored with extract from lobster shell) -> part_of -> lobster and pulled in the whole 73-node lobster subtree. Direction is now `inverse`; this test fails if it is ever flipped back.

cases.name: shellfish DOES reach the lobster-flavoured soybean oil
expect: soybean oil (flavored with extract from lobster shell)
cases.reject_note: the correct direction for the same edge: avoiding lobster should flag the oil, avoiding soy should not flag lobster

cases.name: REGRESSION pepper reaches paprika and the deep cultivars
cases.why: A shared depth budget of 6, counted from the query root, put `hungarian wax pepper plant` at the edge of it: its food products were never traversed, so a `pepper` query returned 147 classes and no paprika while the narrower `Capsicum` returned 177 and found it. The same cap also cut 19 real pepper cultivars out of the taxonomic phase. Phase 1 and phase 2 now hold separate budgets, each counted from where that phase starts.

cases.name: INVARIANT fish does not reach shellfish
cases.why: FALCPA treats fish and crustacean shellfish as SEPARATE allergens. Before the unionOf fix both queries returned the same 4,508 classes, because `owl:unionOf` operands were read as superclasses: a mutual is_a is an equivalence, and that collapsed the aquatic-animal groupings into one class.

cases.name: INVARIANT shellfish does not reach fish
cases.why: The other direction of the same defect.

cases.name: INVARIANT tree nut does not reach cereal grains or legumes
cases.why: `plant seed or nut food product` was asserted both as a subclass and a superclass of `nut food product`, so a tree-nut query descended into every plant seed and returned 2,176 classes including rice and soy. Now 399.

cases.name: egg spans every bird egg, and no embryology
cases.why: Egg allergy is to proteins every bird egg carries, so `animal egg` is a root alongside the component-level class. Before the unionOf fix `animal egg` was reachable only through the inverted edge `animal egg is_a shelled egg`; correcting that lost quail, goose, ostrich egg and animal roe until the root was added. The 12 UBERON embryology stages that also sit under `animal egg` are excluded by config/relation_policy.json rather than by narrowing the root -- they are the only non-food members of that subtree.

cases.name: citrus reaches the plant side, and stops at the family
cases.why: FoodOn's plant hierarchy has no genus-level citrus class: seventeen plant classes hang off `citrus family`, which is Rutaceae and therefore ABOVE the genus. Six carry `in taxon <species>` and were reachable; eleven did not and were not, so a citrus query returned 308 classes and reached neither `lemon plant` nor `orange plant`. Five signed `in taxon` links in config/taxon-bridges.json close it, one class at a time and on FoodOn's own property. The rejects are why it is done per class rather than by bridging `citrus family` wholesale: Zanthoxylum -- prickly ash, japan pepper, sansho, uzazi -- is in the family and is not citrus, and the family node itself stays out because reaching it would be an ascent.

cases.name: a dish is not the parent of its cooking method
cases.why: FoodOn defines `Buffalo wing (dish) = prepared chicken wing and (food (baked) or food (deep-fried))`. The union sits INSIDE an intersection, which entails `Buffalo wing subClassOf (baked or fried)` and nothing whatever about `food (baked) subClassOf Buffalo wing`. Reading those operands as children made a chicken dish the parent of every baked food, so poultry returned 1,200 classes instead of 875 and egg returned 1,160 instead of 882 -- both swallowing the entire baked-goods tree, 327 classes of it. The top-level `X = A or B` rule that makes operands children is right and does not apply once a union is nested inside an intersection.
